grandparents_cupboard.reason: Flour, butter, a Bramley, cheddar, milk, egg, salt and thyme are all plain kitchen staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at Tesco at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, grater, knife and baking tray, and rubbing in and patting out a scone round is within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 350g self-raising flour to 85g butter and 150ml milk is a standard scone ratio once the moist apple is counted, 3cm wedges at 220°C for 15 to 18 minutes will bake through, and 8 scones suits four people as a snack.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes covers rubbing in, peeling and dicing one apple, grating the cheese and shaping, and the 18 minute cook matches the bake in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed item, including the salt, the fresh thyme and the egg for glazing, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Stored Bramleys suit late February, and the diced apple runs right through the dough rather than sitting on top as a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no fuss or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Cheese and apple scones are a filling, real-food afternoon snack a family would happily make again.
